audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 2 Samuel chapter 14, first-pass draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for Joab's scripted widow, blood-revenge narrative, royal flattery, manipulation, return without accountability, appearance praise, hair weight, daughter Tamar, prolonged exclusion, arson, death-or-access demand, and performative reconciliation.

verses.restored: Joab son of Zeruiah knew heart of king was toward Absalom.

familiar.text: Now Joab the son of Zeruiah perceived that the king’s heart was toward Absalom.

modern.text: Now Joab son of Zeruiah perceived that the king’s heart longed for Absalom.

original.text: וַיֵּ֖דַע יוֹאָ֣ב בֶּן צְרֻיָ֑ה כִּֽי לֵ֥ב הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ עַל אַבְשָׁלֽוֹם

verses.restored: Joab sent to Tekoa and brought from there a wise woman. He said, Please present yourself as a mourner, wear mourning garments, do not anoint with oil, and be like a woman mourning many days for the dead.

familiar.text: And Joab sent to Tekoah, and fetched thence a wise woman, and said unto her, I pray thee, feign thyself to be a mourner, and put on now mourning apparel, and anoint not thyself with oil, but be as a woman that had a long time mourned for the dead:

modern.text: So Joab sent to Tekoa to bring a wise woman from there. He told her, “Please pretend to be a mourner; put on clothes for mourning and do not anoint yourself with oil. Act like a woman who has mourned for the dead a long time.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח יוֹאָב֙ תְּק֔וֹעָה וַיִּקַּ֥ח מִשָּׁ֖ם אִשָּׁ֣ה חֲכָמָ֑ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵ֠לֶיהָ הִֽתְאַבְּלִי נָ֞א וְלִבְשִׁי נָ֣א בִגְדֵי אֵ֗בֶל וְאַל תָּס֨וּכִי֙ שֶׁ֔מֶן וְהָיִ֕ית כְּאִשָּׁ֗ה זֶ֚ה יָמִ֣ים רַבִּ֔ים מִתְאַבֶּ֖לֶת עַל מֵֽת

verses.restored: Come to king and speak to him according to this word. Joab placed words in her mouth.

familiar.text: And come to the king, and speak on this manner unto him. So Joab put the words in her mouth.

modern.text: Then go to the king and speak these words to him.” And Joab put the words in her mouth.

original.text: וּבָאת֙ אֶל הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְדִבַּ֥רְתְּ אֵלָ֖יו כַּדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה וַיָּ֧שֶׂם יוֹאָ֛ב אֶת הַדְּבָרִ֖ים בְּפִֽיהָ

verses.restored: Woman of Tekoa spoke to king, fell on her face to ground, bowed, and said, Save, O king.

familiar.text: And when the woman of Tekoah spake to the king, she fell on her face to the ground, and did obeisance, and said, Help, O king.

modern.text: When the woman from Tekoa went to the king, she fell facedown in homage and said, “Help me, O king!”

original.text: וַ֠תֹּאמֶר הָאִשָּׁ֤ה הַתְּקֹעִית֙ אֶל הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַתִּפֹּ֧ל עַל אַפֶּ֛יהָ אַ֖רְצָה וַתִּשְׁתָּ֑חוּ וַתֹּ֖אמֶר הוֹשִׁ֥עָה הַמֶּֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: King said to her, What is it with you? She said, Truly I am a widow; my husband is dead.

familiar.text: And the king said unto her, What aileth thee? And she answered, I am indeed a widow woman, and mine husband is dead.

modern.text: “What troubles you?” the king asked her. “Indeed,” she said, “I am a widow, for my husband is dead.

original.text: וַיֹּֽאמֶר לָ֥הּ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ מַה לָּ֑ךְ וַתֹּ֗אמֶר אֲבָ֛ל אִשָּֽׁה אַלְמָנָ֥ה אָ֖נִי וַיָּ֥מָת אִישִֽׁי

verses.restored: Your maidservant had two sons. Two struggled in field, and no one separated them. One struck the other and killed him.

familiar.text: And thy handmaid had two sons, and they two strove together in the field, and there was none to part them, but the one smote the other, and slew him.

modern.text: And your maidservant had two sons who were fighting in the field with no one to separate them, and one struck the other and killed him.

original.text: וּלְשִׁפְחָֽתְךָ֙ שְׁנֵ֣י בָנִ֔ים וַיִּנָּצ֤וּ שְׁנֵיהֶם֙ בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה וְאֵ֥ין מַצִּ֖יל בֵּֽינֵיהֶ֑ם וַיַּכּ֧וֹ הָאֶחָ֛ד אֶת הָאֶחָ֖ד וַיָּ֥מֶת אֹתֽוֹ

verses.restored: Look, whole clan has risen against your maidservant and says, Give the one who struck his brother, that we may put him to death for life of his brother whom he killed, and destroy heir also. They would extinguish my remaining coal and leave my husband neither name nor remnant upon face of ground.

familiar.text: And, behold, the whole family is risen against thine handmaid, and they said, Deliver him that smote his brother, that we may kill him, for the life of his brother whom he slew; and we will destroy the heir also: and so they shall quench my coal which is left, and shall not leave to my husband neither name nor remainder upon the earth.

modern.text: Now the whole clan has risen up against your maidservant and said, ‘Hand over the one who struck down his brother, that we may put him to death for the life of the brother whom he killed. Then we will cut off the heir as well!’ So they would extinguish my one remaining ember by not preserving my husband’s name or posterity on the earth.”

original.text: וְהִנֵּה֩ קָ֨מָה כָֽל הַמִּשְׁפָּחָ֜ה עַל שִׁפְחָתֶ֗ךָ וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ תְּנִ֣י אֶת מַכֵּ֣ה אָחִ֗יו וּנְמִתֵ֨הוּ֙ בְּנֶ֤פֶשׁ אָחִיו֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָרָ֔ג וְנַשְׁמִ֖ידָה גַּ֣ם אֶת הַיּוֹרֵ֑שׁ וְכִבּ֗וּ אֶת גַּֽחַלְתִּי֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִשְׁאָ֔רָה לְבִלְתִּ֧י שום לְאִישִׁ֛י שֵׁ֥ם וּשְׁאֵרִ֖ית עַל פְּנֵ֥י הָאֲדָמָֽה

verses.restored: King said to woman, Go to your house, and I will command concerning you.

familiar.text: And the king said unto the woman, Go to thine house, and I will give charge concerning thee.

modern.text: “Go home,” the king said to the woman, “and I will give orders on your behalf.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ אֶל הָאִשָּׁ֖ה לְכִ֣י לְבֵיתֵ֑ךְ וַאֲנִ֖י אֲצַוֶּ֥ה עָלָֽיִךְ

verses.restored: Woman of Tekoa said to king, Upon me, my lord king, be guilt, and upon house of my father; king and his throne are innocent.

familiar.text: And the woman of Tekoah said unto the king, My lord, O king, the iniquity be on me, and on my father’s house: and the king and his throne be guiltless.

modern.text: But the woman of Tekoa said to the king, “My lord the king, may any blame be on me and on my father’s house, and may the king and his throne be guiltless.”

original.text: וַתֹּ֜אמֶר הָאִשָּׁ֤ה הַתְּקוֹעִית֙ אֶל הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ עָלַ֞י אֲדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ הֶעָוֺ֖ן וְעַל בֵּ֣ית אָבִ֑י וְהַמֶּ֥לֶךְ וְכִסְא֖וֹ נָקִֽי

verses.restored: King said, Whoever speaks to you, bring him to me, and he shall not touch you again.

familiar.text: And the king said, Whosoever saith ought unto thee, bring him to me, and he shall not touch thee any more.

modern.text: “If anyone speaks to you,” said the king, “bring him to me, and he will not trouble you again!”

original.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ הַֽמְדַבֵּ֤ר אֵלַ֨יִךְ֙ וַֽהֲבֵאת֣וֹ אֵלַ֔י וְלֹֽא יֹסִ֥יף ע֖וֹד לָגַ֥עַת בָּֽךְ

verses.restored: She said, Please let king remember YHWH your Divine, so avenger of blood does not increase destruction and they do not destroy my son. He said, As YHWH lives, not one hair of your son shall fall to ground.

familiar.text: Then said she, I pray thee, let the king remember the LORD thy God, that thou wouldest not suffer the revengers of blood to destroy any more, lest they destroy my son. And he said, As the LORD liveth, there shall not one hair of thy son fall to the earth.

modern.text: “Please,” she replied, “may the king invoke the LORD your God to prevent the avenger of blood from increasing the devastation, so that my son may not be destroyed!” “As surely as the LORD lives,” he vowed, “not a hair of your son’s head will fall to the ground.”

original.text: וַתֹּאמֶר֩ יִזְכָּר נָ֨א הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אֶת יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֗יךָ מהרבית גֹּאֵ֤ל הַדָּם֙ לְשַׁחֵ֔ת וְלֹ֥א יַשְׁמִ֖ידוּ אֶת בְּנִ֑י וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ חַי יְהוָ֔ה אִם יִפֹּ֛ל מִשַּׂעֲרַ֥ת בְּנֵ֖ךְ אָֽרְצָה

verses.restored: Woman said, Please let your maidservant speak a word to my lord king. He said, Speak.

familiar.text: Then the woman said, Let thine handmaid, I pray thee, speak one word unto my lord the king. And he said, Say on.

modern.text: Then the woman said, “Please, may your servant speak a word to my lord the king?” “Speak,” he replied.

original.text: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה תְּדַבֶּר נָ֧א שִׁפְחָתְךָ֛ אֶל אֲדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ דָּבָ֑ר וַיֹּ֖אמֶר דַּבֵּֽרִי

verses.restored: Woman said, Why then have you planned such a thing against people of Divine? By speaking this word king is like one guilty, in not returning his banished one.

familiar.text: And the woman said, Wherefore then hast thou thought such a thing against the people of God? for the king doth speak this thing as one which is faulty, in that the king doth not fetch home again his banished.

modern.text: The woman asked, “Why have you devised a thing like this against the people of God? When the king says this, does he not convict himself, since he has not brought back his own banished son?

original.text: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה וְלָ֧מָּה חָשַׁ֛בְתָּה כָּזֹ֖את עַל עַ֣ם אֱלֹהִ֑ים וּמִדַּבֵּ֨ר הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ הַדָּבָ֤ר הַזֶּה֙ כְּאָשֵׁ֔ם לְבִלְתִּ֛י הָשִׁ֥יב הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶֽת נִדְּחֽוֹ

verses.restored: We surely die and are like water spilled to ground that cannot be gathered. Divine does not take away life but devises means so banished one is not banished from Divine.

familiar.text: For we must needs die, and are as water spilt on the ground, which cannot be gathered up again; neither doth God respect any person: yet doth he devise means, that his banished be not expelled from him.

modern.text: For surely we will die and be like water poured out on the ground, which cannot be recovered. Yet God does not take away a life; but He devises ways that the banished one may not be cast out from Him.

original.text: כִּי מ֣וֹת נָמ֔וּת וְכַמַּ֨יִם֙ הַנִּגָּרִ֣ים אַ֔רְצָה אֲשֶׁ֖ר לֹ֣א יֵאָסֵ֑פוּ וְלֹֽא יִשָּׂ֤א אֱלֹהִים֙ נֶ֔פֶשׁ וְחָשַׁב֙ מַֽחֲשָׁב֔וֹת לְבִלְתִּ֛י יִדַּ֥ח מִמֶּ֖נּוּ נִדָּֽח

verses.restored: Now I came to speak this word to my lord king because people made me afraid. Your maidservant said, I will speak to king; perhaps king will perform word of his maidservant.

familiar.text: Now therefore that I am come to speak of this thing unto my lord the king, it is because the people have made me afraid: and thy handmaid said, I will now speak unto the king; it may be that the king will perform the request of his handmaid.

modern.text: Now therefore, I have come to present this matter to my lord the king because the people have made me afraid. Your servant thought, ‘I will speak to the king. Perhaps he will grant the request of his maidservant.

original.text: וְ֠עַתָּה אֲשֶׁר בָּ֜אתִי לְדַבֵּ֨ר אֶל הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ אֲדֹנִי֙ אֶת הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה כִּ֥י יֵֽרְאֻ֖נִי הָעָ֑ם וַתֹּ֤אמֶר שִׁפְחָֽתְךָ֙ אֲדַבְּרָה נָּ֣א אֶל הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אוּלַ֛י יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶת דְּבַ֥ר אֲמָתֽוֹ

verses.restored: For king will listen, to rescue his maidservant from hand of man seeking to destroy me and my son together from inheritance of Divine.

familiar.text: For the king will hear, to deliver his handmaid out of the hand of the man that would destroy me and my son together out of the inheritance of God.

modern.text: For the king will hear and deliver his maidservant from the hand of the man who would cut off both me and my son from God’s inheritance.’

original.text: כִּ֚י יִשְׁמַ֣ע הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לְהַצִּ֥יל אֶת אֲמָת֖וֹ מִכַּ֣ף הָאִ֑ישׁ לְהַשְׁמִ֨יד אֹתִ֤י וְאֶת בְּנִי֙ יַ֔חַד מִֽנַּחֲלַ֖ת אֱלֹהִֽים

verses.restored: Your maidservant said, Let word of my lord king give rest, because like messenger of Divine is my lord king to hear good and evil. May YHWH your Divine be with you.

familiar.text: Then thine handmaid said, The word of my lord the king shall now be comfortable: for as an angel of God, so is my lord the king to discern good and bad: therefore the LORD thy God will be with thee.

modern.text: And now your servant says, ‘May the word of my lord the king bring me rest, for my lord the king is able to discern good and evil, just like the angel of God. May the LORD your God be with you.’”

original.text: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ שִׁפְחָ֣תְךָ֔ יִֽהְיֶה נָּ֛א דְּבַר אֲדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ לִמְנוּחָ֑ה כִּ֣י כְּמַלְאַ֣ךְ הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים כֵּ֣ן אֲדֹנִ֤י הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ לִשְׁמֹ֨עַ֙ הַטּ֣וֹב וְהָרָ֔ע וַֽיהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ יְהִ֥י עִמָּֽךְ

verses.restored: King answered and said to woman, Please do not hide from me a thing I ask you. Woman said, Please let my lord king speak.

familiar.text: Then the king answered and said unto the woman, Hide not from me, I pray thee, the thing that I shall ask thee. And the woman said, Let my lord the king now speak.

modern.text: Then the king said to the woman, “I am going to ask you something; do not conceal it from me!” “Let my lord the king speak,” she replied.

original.text: וַיַּ֣עַן הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל הָ֣אִשָּׁ֔ה אַל נָ֨א תְכַחֲדִ֤י מִמֶּ֨נִּי֙ דָּבָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָנֹכִ֖י שֹׁאֵ֣ל אֹתָ֑ךְ וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה יְדַבֶּר נָ֖א אֲדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: King said, Is hand of Joab with you in all this? Woman answered, By life of your soul, my lord king, no one can turn right or left from all my lord king has spoken. Your servant Joab commanded me and placed all these words in mouth of your maidservant.

familiar.text: And the king said, Is not the hand of Joab with thee in all this? And the woman answered and said, As thy soul liveth, my lord the king, none can turn to the right hand or to the left from ought that my lord the king hath spoken: for thy servant Joab, he bade me, and he put all these words in the mouth of thine handmaid:

modern.text: So the king asked, “Is the hand of Joab behind all this?” The woman answered, “As surely as you live, my lord the king, no one can turn to the right or to the left from anything that my lord the king says. Yes, your servant Joab is the one who gave me orders; he told your maidservant exactly what to say.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ הֲיַ֥ד יוֹאָ֛ב אִתָּ֖ךְ בְּכָל זֹ֑את וַתַּ֣עַן הָאִשָּׁ֣ה וַתֹּ֡אמֶר חֵֽי נַפְשְׁךָ֩ אֲדֹנִ֨י הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אִם אִ֣שׁ לְהֵמִ֣ין וּלְהַשְׂמִ֗יל מִכֹּ֤ל אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר֙ אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ כִּֽי עַבְדְּךָ֤ יוֹאָב֙ ה֣וּא צִוָּ֔נִי וְה֗וּא שָׂ֚ם בְּפִ֣י שִׁפְחָֽתְךָ֔ אֵ֥ת כָּל הַדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵֽלֶּה

verses.restored: To turn face/form of matter your servant Joab did this thing. My lord is wise like wisdom of messenger of Divine, knowing all that is in land.

familiar.text: To fetch about this form of speech hath thy servant Joab done this thing: and my lord is wise, according to the wisdom of an angel of God, to know all things that are in the earth.

modern.text: Joab your servant has done this to bring about this change of affairs, but my lord has wisdom like the wisdom of the angel of God, to know everything that happens in the land.”

original.text: לְבַעֲב֤וּר סַבֵּב֙ אֶת פְּנֵ֣י הַדָּבָ֔ר עָשָׂ֛ה עַבְדְּךָ֥ יוֹאָ֖ב אֶת הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה וַאדֹנִ֣י חָכָ֗ם כְּחָכְמַת֙ מַלְאַ֣ךְ הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים לָדַ֖עַת אֶֽת כָּל אֲשֶׁ֥ר בָּאָֽרֶץ

verses.restored: King said to Joab, Look, I have done this thing. Go and return young man Absalom.

familiar.text: And the king said unto Joab, Behold now, I have done this thing: go therefore, bring the young man Absalom again.

modern.text: Then the king said to Joab, “I hereby grant this request. Go, bring back the young man Absalom.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ אֶל יוֹאָ֔ב הִנֵּה נָ֥א עָשִׂ֖יתִי אֶת הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה וְלֵ֛ךְ הָשֵׁ֥ב אֶת הַנַּ֖עַר אֶת אַבְשָׁלֽוֹם

verses.restored: Joab fell on his face to ground, bowed, and blessed king. Joab said, Today your servant knows I found favor in your eyes, my lord king, because king performed request of his servant.

familiar.text: And Joab fell to the ground on his face, and bowed himself, and thanked the king: and Joab said, To day thy servant knoweth that I have found grace in thy sight, my lord, O king, in that the king hath fulfilled the request of his servant.

modern.text: Joab fell facedown in homage and blessed the king. “Today,” said Joab, “your servant knows that he has found favor with you, my lord the king, because the king has granted his request.”

original.text: וַיִּפֹּל֩ יוֹאָ֨ב אֶל פָּנָ֥יו אַ֛רְצָה וַיִּשְׁתַּ֖חוּ וַיְבָ֣רֶךְ אֶת הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יוֹאָ֡ב הַיּוֹם֩ יָדַ֨ע עַבְדְּךָ֜ כִּי מָצָ֨אתִי חֵ֤ן בְּעֵינֶ֨יךָ֙ אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂ֥ה הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶת דְּבַ֥ר עבדו

verses.restored: Joab arose, went to Geshur, and brought Absalom to Jerusalem.

familiar.text: So Joab arose and went to Geshur, and brought Absalom to Jerusalem.

modern.text: So Joab got up, went to Geshur, and brought Absalom to Jerusalem.

original.text: וַיָּ֥קָם יוֹאָ֖ב וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ גְּשׁ֑וּרָה וַיָּבֵ֥א אֶת אַבְשָׁל֖וֹם יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם

verses.restored: King said, Let him turn to his house, and he shall not see my face. Absalom turned to his house and did not see face of king.

familiar.text: And the king said, Let him turn to his own house, and let him not see my face. So Absalom returned to his own house, and saw not the king’s face.

modern.text: But the king added, “He may return to his house, but he must not see my face.” So Absalom returned to his own house, but he did not see the king.

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ יִסֹּ֣ב אֶל בֵּית֔וֹ וּפָנַ֖י לֹ֣א יִרְאֶ֑ה וַיִּסֹּ֤ב אַבְשָׁלוֹם֙ אֶל בֵּית֔וֹ וּפְנֵ֥י הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ לֹ֥א רָאָֽה

verses.restored: In all Israel there was no man greatly praised for beauty like Absalom. From sole of his foot to crown of his head there was no blemish in him.

familiar.text: But in all Israel there was none to be so much praised as Absalom for his beauty: from the sole of his foot even to the crown of his head there was no blemish in him.

modern.text: Now there was not a man in all Israel as handsome and highly praised as Absalom. From the sole of his foot to the top of his head, he did not have a single flaw.

original.text: וּכְאַבְשָׁל֗וֹם לֹא הָיָ֧ה אִישׁ יָפֶ֛ה בְּכָל יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְהַלֵּ֣ל מְאֹ֑ד מִכַּ֤ף רַגְלוֹ֙ וְעַ֣ד קָדְקֳד֔וֹ לֹא הָ֥יָה ב֖וֹ מֽוּם

verses.restored: When he cut hair of his head—at end of days he cut it because it was heavy upon him—he weighed hair of his head: two hundred shekels by royal weight.

familiar.text: And when he polled his head, (for it was at every year’s end that he polled it: because the hair was heavy on him, therefore he polled it:) he weighed the hair of his head at two hundred shekels after the king’s weight.

modern.text: And when he cut the hair of his head—he shaved it every year because his hair got so heavy—he would weigh it out to be two hundred shekels, according to the royal standard.

original.text: וּֽבְגַלְּחוֹ֮ אֶת רֹאשׁוֹ֒ וְֽ֠הָיָה מִקֵּ֨ץ יָמִ֤ים לַיָּמִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יְגַלֵּ֔חַ כִּֽי כָבֵ֥ד עָלָ֖יו וְגִלְּח֑וֹ וְשָׁקַל֙ אֶת שְׂעַ֣ר רֹאשׁ֔וֹ מָאתַ֥יִם שְׁקָלִ֖ים בְּאֶ֥בֶן הַמֶּֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: To Absalom were born three sons and one daughter, whose name was Tamar. She was a woman beautiful in appearance.

familiar.text: And unto Absalom there were born three sons, and one daughter, whose name was Tamar: she was a woman of a fair countenance.

modern.text: Three sons were born to Absalom, and a daughter named Tamar, who was a beautiful woman. Absalom Reconciled to David

original.text: וַיִּֽוָּלְד֤וּ לְאַבְשָׁלוֹם֙ שְׁלוֹשָׁ֣ה בָנִ֔ים וּבַ֥ת אַחַ֖ת וּשְׁמָ֣הּ תָּמָ֑ר הִ֣יא הָיְתָ֔ה אִשָּׁ֖ה יְפַ֥ת מַרְאֶֽה

verses.restored: Absalom lived two full years in Jerusalem and did not see face of king.

familiar.text: So Absalom dwelt two full years in Jerusalem, and saw not the king’s face.

modern.text: Now Absalom lived in Jerusalem two years without seeing the face of the king.

original.text: וַיֵּ֧שֶׁב אַבְשָׁל֛וֹם בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם שְׁנָתַ֣יִם יָמִ֑ים וּפְנֵ֥י הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ לֹ֥א רָאָֽה

verses.restored: Absalom sent for Joab, to send him to king, but Joab was not willing to come. He sent again a second time, but Joab was not willing to come.

familiar.text: Therefore Absalom sent for Joab, to have sent him to the king; but he would not come to him: and when he sent again the second time, he would not come.

modern.text: Then he sent for Joab to send him to the king, but Joab refused to come to him. So Absalom sent a second time, but Joab still would not come.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח אַבְשָׁל֜וֹם אֶל יוֹאָ֗ב לִשְׁלֹ֤חַ אֹתוֹ֙ אֶל הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְלֹ֥א אָבָ֖ה לָב֣וֹא אֵלָ֑יו וַיִּשְׁלַ֥ח עוֹד֙ שֵׁנִ֔ית וְלֹ֥א אָבָ֖ה לָבֽוֹא

verses.restored: He said to his servants, See, Joab's field is near mine and he has barley there. Go and set it on fire. Servants of Absalom set field on fire.

familiar.text: Therefore he said unto his servants, See, Joab’s field is near mine, and he hath barley there; go and set it on fire. And Absalom’s servants set the field on fire.

modern.text: Then Absalom said to his servants, “Look, Joab’s field is next to mine, and he has barley there. Go and set it on fire!” And Absalom’s servants set the field on fire.

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֶל עֲבָדָ֜יו רְאוּ֩ חֶלְקַ֨ת יוֹאָ֤ב אֶל יָדִי֙ וְלוֹ שָׁ֣ם שְׂעֹרִ֔ים לְכ֖וּ והוצתיה בָאֵ֑שׁ וַיַּצִּ֜תוּ עַבְדֵ֧י אַבְשָׁל֛וֹם אֶת הַחֶלְקָ֖ה בָּאֵֽשׁ

verses.restored: Joab arose, came to Absalom at house, and said, Why did your servants set my field on fire?

familiar.text: Then Joab arose, and came to Absalom unto his house, and said unto him, Wherefore have thy servants set my field on fire?

modern.text: Then Joab came to Absalom’s house and demanded, “Why did your servants set my field on fire?”

original.text: וַיָּ֣קָם יוֹאָ֔ב וַיָּבֹ֥א אֶל אַבְשָׁל֖וֹם הַבָּ֑יְתָה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו לָ֣מָּה הִצִּ֧יתוּ עֲבָדֶ֛ךָ אֶת הַחֶלְקָ֥ה אֲשֶׁר לִ֖י בָּאֵֽשׁ

verses.restored: Absalom said to Joab, Look, I sent to you, saying, Come here, that I may send you to king, saying, Why did I come from Geshur? It was better for me to still be there. Now let me see face of king; if guilt is in me, let him put me to death.

familiar.text: And Absalom answered Joab, Behold, I sent unto thee, saying, Come hither, that I may send thee to the king, to say, Wherefore am I come from Geshur? it had been good for me to have been there still: now therefore let me see the king’s face; and if there be any iniquity in me, let him kill me.

modern.text: “Look,” said Absalom, “I sent for you and said, ‘Come here. I want to send you to the king to ask: Why have I come back from Geshur? It would be better for me if I were still there.’ So now, let me see the king’s face, and if there is iniquity in me, let him kill me.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אַבְשָׁל֣וֹם אֶל יוֹאָ֡ב הִנֵּ֣ה שָׁלַ֣חְתִּי אֵלֶ֣יךָ לֵאמֹ֡ר בֹּ֣א הֵ֠נָּה וְאֶשְׁלְחָה֩ אֹתְךָ֨ אֶל הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ לֵאמֹ֗ר לָ֤מָּה בָּ֨אתִי֙ מִגְּשׁ֔וּר ט֥וֹב לִ֖י עֹ֣ד אֲנִי שָׁ֑ם וְעַתָּ֗ה אֶרְאֶה֙ פְּנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְאִם יֶשׁ בִּ֥י עָוֺ֖ן וֶהֱמִתָֽנִי

verses.restored: Joab came to king and told him. He called Absalom; he came to king and bowed on his face to ground before king, and king kissed Absalom.

familiar.text: So Joab came to the king, and told him: and when he had called for Absalom, he came to the king, and bowed himself on his face to the ground before the king: and the king kissed Absalom.

modern.text: So Joab went and told the king, and David summoned Absalom, who came to him and bowed facedown before him. Then the king kissed Absalom.

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֨א יוֹאָ֣ב אֶל הַמֶּלֶךְ֮ וַיַּגֶּד לוֹ֒ וַיִּקְרָ֤א אֶל אַבְשָׁלוֹם֙ וַיָּבֹ֣א אֶל הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַיִּשְׁתַּ֨חוּ ל֧וֹ עַל אַפָּ֛יו אַ֖רְצָה לִפְנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיִּשַּׁ֥ק הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ לְאַבְשָׁלֽוֹם

translation_notes: The wise woman is recruited, costumed, and scripted by Joab. Her rhetorical skill is real, but the situation is engineered by a military commander.

The parable raises legitimate concerns about retaliatory family killing and preserving a widow's household; its application to Absalom is imperfect because Amnon's killing followed Tamar's rape and David's inaction.
Reconciliation is pursued without recorded consultation with Tamar, public truth, accountability for Amnon's rape, accountability for Absalom's execution, or repair for affected servants.
The woman repeatedly flatters David as angelic and all-knowing. Praise under royal power should not be mistaken for objective moral evaluation.
Absalom's return without access creates prolonged ambiguous punishment rather than a transparent justice process.
Praise of Absalom's body and hair is political image-making, not evidence of virtue. 'No blemish' language must not support ableism or beauty hierarchy.
Absalom names his daughter Tamar, preserving the name of his sister, but the text does not tell us what restoration the first Tamar received.
Burning Joab's field is coercive property destruction. Being ignored does not make arson a healthy communication method.
The final kiss is symbolic reunion without evidence of resolved conflict, responsibility, trust, or safety.
safety_note: Do not use this chapter to force family reconciliation, bypass survivors, praise charismatic beauty, or substitute symbolic affection for accountability. Wise mediation must not be scripted to protect dynastic stability at the expense of Tamar's voice and public justice.
